parsed.explanation: No documented criminalisation, entry bar, or universal facility exclusion for trans visitors, and courts repeatedly intervene for trans people with functioning anti-discrimination law and hate-crime prosecutions. This is offset by top-level official hostility, a documented high level of reported discrimination/harassment, and unresolved detention/prison placement: a supreme-court vulnerability safeguard exists but lower-court practice is inconsistent and prison rules remain unprepared and contested. Severity after outing is therefore mainly harassment, bureaucratic/detention vulnerability and inconsistent protection, not imprisonment or execution.

entry_documents.protection: No documented refusal or marker-based entry bar; 2009 anti-discrimination law covers access to goods and services.
entry_documents.interaction: Visitor uses home passport; resident legal-gender reform is only a climate signal, not a direct entry protection.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Detained trans foreigners handled inconsistently by immigration police/lower courts; prisons lack clear rules and are not prepared for trans people.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: 2023 supreme administrative court requires vulnerability assessment before placement; supreme court pressing for explicit trans needs in prison concept.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Safeguard exists at highest court but practice below it remains inconsistent and justice ministry resists binding regulation.

care_services.protection: Anti-discrimination law covers access to goods and services; no documented visitor care denial.
care_services.interaction: Resident sexology/surgical gatekeeping is not a documented visitor-facing exposure.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Head of state in 2021 called trans people disgusting and surgery self-harm crime; justice minister in 2024 aimed to prevent men giving birth; politician anti-LGBT speech rising.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Constitutional court 2024 and regional court 2025 struck surgical/sterilisation condition; anti-discrimination law covers gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile political framing coexists with strong judicial protection, raising social hostility while courts limit state action.

minors_guardians.interaction: No age-dependent visitor rule documented; school-curriculum opt-outs concern residents.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 2023 LGBTQ+ survey: 43% discriminated/harassed in 5 years, highest among trans/non-binary; 51% insults/assault/threats in 5 years; harassment said to concentrate rural/late-night.
street_violence_police_response.protection: 94 hate crimes recorded in 2024, 46 prosecuted, 42 sentenced; statistics admittedly understate bias crime.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Prosecutions show some recourse, but pending bias-crime amendment and weak recording limit reliability; survey is LGBT-wide, 2023, so discounted as trans-specific prevalence.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Prison regulation unresolved, bias-crime amendment pending, 2025 legal-gender reform may be administrative and reversible.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Constitutional, supreme administrative and regional courts have all ruled for trans claimants; regional court ordered reissued documents.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Judicial remedies operate, but legislative/regulatory consolidation is incomplete and practice varies by court/area.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: national protection and higher-court intervention coexist with inconsistent frontline detention practice and brief intrusive handling, with remedies/apology but no imprisonment. This case has stronger court rulings, hence not lower.

Lower than 0.75-D: despite equality protection and prosecutions, documented top-level hostility, unresolved prison/detention placement, and pending hate-crime law make protection less reliably operative than in the anchor.
Materially higher than 0.35-B: no documented routine police stops, extortion, fines or compelled interviews for visitors, and courts actually overturn state practice rather than deferring to police.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: courts and anti-discrimination law provide real, sometimes effective protection, and hate-crime sentences show enforcement, but officials' hostile framing, high reported harassment, and inconsistent detention/prison practice leave an outed visitor exposed to social hostility and vulnerable if detained. No documented universal exposure, organised targeting, imprisonment pathway or lethal risk. Hence elevated-to-reduced risk, near the 0.65 anchor, below jurisdictions with settled facility/custody rules and operative bias-crime law.
